business_model.claim: Okta employs a SaaS business model, generating revenue primarily from multi-year subscriptions to its cloud-based Okta Platform and Auth0 Platform for workforce identity and customer identity.
quotes: We employ a SaaS business model and generate revenue primarily by selling multi-year subscriptions to our cloud-based offerings.

Our platforms are traditionally used by organizations in two distinct ways: “workforce identity”, supported by our Okta Platform, to manage and secure employees, contractors and partners; and “customer identity”, supported by both our Okta Platform and Auth0 Platform, to secure customers.

business_model.claim: The Okta Platform manages access, security, and identity governance for employees, contractors, partners, and non-human identities, while the developer-centric Auth0 Platform embeds identity into customer- and citizen-facing applications, with both expanding to address AI agents.
quotes: The Okta Platform governs and simplifies the way an organization’s employees, contractors, partners and NHIs connect to applications and data from any device.

The Auth0 Platform is developer-centric and enables companies, nonprofits and governmental agencies to rapidly embed secure, extensible identity management into customer- and citizen-facing cloud, mobile, and web applications.
We are extending our platforms to address the unique identity security challenges posed by AI agents.

business_model.claim: Subscription revenue—covering platform access, technical support, and platform management—constituted approximately 98% of total revenue in fiscal 2026 ($2,855 of $2,919, table in millions) and 98% in the six months ended July 31, 2026 ($1,543 of 1,570, table in millions).
quotes: Our subscription fees include the use of our service and our technical support and management of our platforms.
Our revenue is relatively predictable as a result of our subscription-based business model, which constituted approximately 98% of total revenue for fiscal 2026.
Our revenue is relatively predictable as a result of our subscription-based business model, which constituted 98% of total revenue for the six months ended July 31, 2026.

quotes: Professional services revenue includes fees from assisting customers in implementing and optimizing the use of our solutions.
These services include application configuration, system integration and training services.
The cost of providing professional services has historically been higher than the associated revenue we generate.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Okta faces intense competition from larger, better-resourced rivals—principally Microsoft—that can bundle identity functionality into broader products, price at zero or negative margins, or maintain closed platforms to discourage purchases of Okta's solutions.
quotes: We face intense competition, especially from larger, well-established companies, and we may lack sufficient financial or other resources to maintain or improve our competitive position.
Our principal competitor is Microsoft.

As a result, they can leverage their relationships based on other solutions, or incorporate functionality into existing solutions, to gain business in a manner that discourages users from purchasing our solutions, including selling at zero or negative margins, bundling products or maintaining closed technology platforms.

These competitive pressures or our failure to compete effectively may result in price reductions, fewer orders, reduced revenue and gross margins, increased net losses and loss of market share, which could harm our business, results of operations and financial condition.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Larger competitors and acquired startups spend considerably more on research and development and may introduce competing or AI-integrated offerings faster or give equivalent features away for free, threatening Okta's ability to recoup its R&D investments.
quotes: Further, many of our competitors expend a considerably greater amount of funds on their respective research and development programs, and those that do not have, in some cases, been acquired by larger companies that allocate greater resources to our competitors’ research and development programs.

For example, if we develop a new feature but our competitors give an equivalent feature away for free, we may need to also include our newly developed feature for free as part of an existing product offering to remain competitive in the marketplace.

It is also possible that products and services developed by others, including, but not limited to, new technologies and offerings integrating AI, or products and services developed by competitors, could put us at a competitive disadvantage.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 Item 1A Risk Factors, P3 Item 7 MD&A, and P4 Item 2 MD&A)
competitive_position.claim: Past cybersecurity incidents—including a January 2022 third-party service provider incident and an October 2023 breach of its third-party customer support system—harmed Okta's reputation, customer relations, and financial results, and future incidents or customer sentiment could reduce retention and expansion.
quotes: In the past we have experienced cybersecurity incidents, such as the January 2022 incident involving one of our third-party service providers and the October 2023 incident where a threat actor gained unauthorized access to and stole information from our third-party customer support system, that harmed our reputation and customer relations and adversely impacted our financial results.
We and our third-party service providers may experience similar incidents in the future which may also include disabling access to our service.
Due to the nature of our business, the announcement of any security incidents, even if not significant, could have these impacts.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Okta's competitiveness is exposed to interoperability, ecosystem, and implementation risks because it depends on third-party operating systems and applications remaining compatible, third-party developers continuing to support its APIs, and partners—some of whom also compete with Okta—successfully selling and deploying its solutions.
quotes: If we are unable to ensure that our solutions integrate or interoperate with a variety of operating systems, platforms, services, software applications devices, mobile phones and other hardware form factors that are developed by others, our platforms may become less competitive and our results of operations may be harmed.
Some of our partners compete with certain of our solutions and may elect to no longer integrate with our platforms or sell our solutions.
If these third-party developers stop developing on or supporting our platforms, we will lose the benefit of network effects that have contributed to the growth in our number of customers.

Unsuccessful, lengthy or costly customer implementation and integration projects could result in claims from customers, harm to our reputation and opportunities for competitors to displace our solutions, each of which could have an adverse effect on our business and results of operations.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 1 Business of the 2026 Form 10-K.
growth_thesis.claim: Digital transformation, cloud adoption, and shifting to Zero Trust security models drive demand for Okta's identity management solutions.
quotes: The acceleration of digital transformation, cloud adoption and the evolving security threat landscape continue to drive a shift in how organizations securely manage the identity of their employees, contractors and partners.

As organizations shift from network-based security models to a Zero Trust security model focused on adaptive and context-aware controls, identity has become the most reliable way to manage user access and protect digital assets.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 1A Risk Factors and Item 7 MD&A of the 2026 Form 10-K and Item 2 MD&A of the Q2 FY27 Form 10-Q.

growth_thesis.claim: Subscription revenue growth has been driven primarily by existing customers adding users and buying additional solutions, reflected in a Dollar-Based Net Retention Rate of 106%.
quotes: For fiscal 2026, the increase in subscription revenue was primarily due to an increase in users and sales of additional solutions to existing customers and the addition of new customers.

The increase in revenue was attributable to increased revenue from existing customers as reflected in our Dollar-Based Net Retention Rate of 106% as of January 31, 2026 and an increase in the number of customers as detailed in our Key Business Metrics.

growth_thesis.claim: For existing-customer expansion to continue, customers must renew expiring subscriptions, maintain or increase user counts, and buy additional products despite competitive or macro pressures.
quotes: This requires that our existing customers continue to use our platforms, either by purchasing additional subscriptions or by renewing their subscriptions when existing contract terms expire.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 1A Risk Factors of the 2026 Form 10-K and Item 2 MD&A of the Q2 FY27 Form 10-Q.

quotes: Our principal competitor is Microsoft.

Future growth may be impacted by longer sales cycles, which we have experienced, which in turn, could result in delays in deals closing, creating near-term headwinds for cash flow, RPO and current RPO growth as well as potential future impacts on revenue growth and other key metrics on a trailing basis.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q2 FY27 earnings release and Item 1 Business of the 2026 Form 10-K.

We see a potential long-term opportunity for our platforms to serve as a unified, independent control plane for non-human identities (“NHIs”) and AI agents, a distinct class of identity that requires authenticated, secure access to sensitive resources at a scale and speed exceeding traditional security models designed for human users.

While adoption is in its early stages, we believe the inherent challenges of governing NHIs and agentic identities may drive increased demand for our solutions as these technologies and customer adoption continue to mature.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 1A Risk Factors of the 2026 Form 10-K.

quotes: Any delay or failure in the introduction of new or enhanced solutions that gain market acceptance and meet customer requirements could harm our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Even if we maintain adequate research and development resources, we may be unable to monetize newly developed solutions or features such that we can recoup our research and development expenditures.

For example, if we develop a new feature but our competitors give an equivalent feature away for free, we may need to also include our newly developed feature for free as part of an existing product offering to remain competitive in the marketplace.
